title: Priyanka Chopra Told Cannes She Hasn't Even Started in Hollywood — and She Meant Every Word
excerpt: At Cannes Lions, India's biggest global export declared her 'next reinvention,' teased a comedy with Zac Efron, and casually announced she's about to be in 200 languages.
body:
There's a particular kind of confidence that comes from someone who's already conquered one industry and is calmly announcing they're about to do it again. **Priyanka Chopra Jonas** brought that energy to Cannes Lions last week, standing on one of the world's most prestigious stages and delivering a line that would be delusional coming from anyone else: she hasn't worked with the best yet.

Not in India. In Hollywood.

> "In my Hindi-language career, I've worked with all the best filmmakers and the best actors, I've told amazing stories and done a variety of genres. Whereas in America, in Hollywood, in my English-language work, I haven't really done that as much." — Priyanka Chopra Jonas

Let that settle for a moment. This is a woman with *Quantico*, *Citadel*, *The Matrix Resurrections*, *Heads of State*, and a number-one Prime Video hit (*The Bluff*) on her résumé. And she's saying this is the warm-up.

She called it her "next reinvention" — the deliberate pursuit of the same depth, the same range, the same calibre of collaborations that defined her Bollywood career. Not more action franchises. Not more supporting roles in ensemble casts. The full spectrum. The kind of work that wins awards and shifts culture.

## The Pipeline Is Already Loaded

And she's already building it. An untitled comedy for **Amazon MGM Studios** reunites her with *Baywatch* co-star **Zac Efron**, alongside **Will Ferrell**, **Michael Peña**, and **Regina Hall**. Written and directed by **Nicholas Stoller** — the mind behind *Neighbors* and *You're Cordially Invited* — the film follows a convict who takes an unscripted TV courtroom hostage. It's the kind of sharp, commercial ensemble Priyanka has rarely been handed in America, and she clearly intends for it to be the first of many.

Then there's the project that connects both of her worlds: **SS Rajamouli's *Varanasi***, a Telugu-language epic co-starring **Mahesh Babu** and **Prithviraj Sukumaran**, set to be dubbed into nearly 200 languages. It's the kind of global-scale Indian cinema Priyanka has been advocating for since she first crossed over — and now she's starring in the definitive version of it.

## Ideas Are the New Currency

At Cannes, she framed her career within a larger argument about the democratisation of entertainment. She pointed to *Obsession* — the $750,000 horror film that just crossed $371 million worldwide — as proof that traditional gatekeepers no longer control who gets to tell stories.

> "What a wonderful time to be an entertainer, to be in the entertainment business, because ideas are your currency. It used to be such a niche industry when I first started." — Priyanka Chopra Jonas

She also credited streaming platforms with making non-English content a global force. "My mom loves Korean dramas. She would never have had access to those if it wasn't for streaming," she said, citing *Squid Game* and *Parasite* as watershed moments. For the diaspora, this argument hits differently — Indian families in Houston and Toronto and London are already living in this post-language-barrier world, watching Malayalam thrillers one night and Korean rom-coms the next.

## The OG Crossover

This matters because **Priyanka was the first**. The Miss World who became a Bollywood queen, then an American network television lead, then a Hollywood film presence, then a producer who could greenlight her own projects. Every Indian actor who gets a seat at a global table — from **Radhika Apte** on Apple TV+ to **Ali Fazal** headlining Prime Video's biggest Indian hit — owes a debt to the door she kicked open with *Quantico* in 2015. And now she's saying the real work is just beginning.

But here's the sharpest shift in her story: motherhood has rewritten the calculus. She's no longer the actress who packed a bag and flew to three continents for five films a year.

> "I don't just pack my bags and go off for a movie anymore. I'm really, really selective about the time I spend and who I spend it with. I'm navigating working-mom life. I have so much more respect for my mother now." — Priyanka Chopra Jonas

Her daughter **Malti Marie** — with husband **Nick Jonas** — has transformed what she'll say yes to. Fewer projects, higher stakes, more control. She's producing through **Purple Pebble Pictures**, backing regional Indian films and opening doors for filmmakers who don't have industry connections — exactly the kind of support she never had as the daughter of two Army doctors with no ties to cinema.

With a Zac Efron comedy in the pipeline, Rajamouli's most ambitious project yet in production, and the declared intention to reinvent her Hollywood career from scratch, Priyanka Chopra Jonas isn't slowing down. She's just getting more dangerous.

**Where to watch Priyanka next:** *The Bluff* and *Heads of State* are streaming now on **Amazon Prime Video** worldwide. *Citadel* Season 2 is expected later in 2026. *Varanasi* is currently in production.
